name: cec_msg_clear_digital_timer
prose: Builds a CEC Clear Digital Timer message in *msg. It sets msg->len = 16; msg->reply = CEC_MSG_TIMER_CLEARED_STATUS if reply is nonzero and 0 otherwise; msg->msg[1] = CEC_MSG_CLEAR_DIGITAL_TIMER; msg->msg[2] = day and msg->msg[3] = month unchanged; msg->msg[4] to msg->msg[7] = start_hr, start_min, duration_hr and duration_min each converted to BCD as ((x / 10) << 4) | (x % 10) and stored in a __u8 (so values of 100 or more are truncated); msg->msg[8] = recording_seq; and then cec_set_digital_service_id(msg->msg + 9, digital), which writes 7 bytes at msg->msg[9..15]: a first byte (service_id_method << 7) | dig_bcast_system, then six bytes holding, by channel, the channel number format with major and minor numbers and zeros, or for ATSC systems the transport id and program number followed by two zero bytes, or otherwise the DVB transport id, service id and original network id. msg->msg[0] and bytes beyond index 15 are not written. digital must be non-NULL.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is cec_msg_clear_digital_timer (include/uapi/linux/cec-funcs.h); the old prose said the BCD times occupy bytes 2-8, but bytes 2 and 3 are the plain day and month, BCD is bytes 4-7, byte 8 is recording_seq; it also missed msg->reply.

name: PISP_IMAGE_FORMAT_BPS
prose: Function-like macro: expands to (((fmt) & PISP_IMAGE_FORMAT_BPS_MASK) ? 8 + (2 << (((fmt) & PISP_IMAGE_FORMAT_BPS_MASK) - 1)) : 8). With PISP_IMAGE_FORMAT_BPS_MASK equal to 3, the low two bits of fmt select the value: 0 gives 8, 1 gives 10, 2 gives 12 and 3 gives 16 (the bits per sample). Other bits of fmt are ignored. fmt is evaluated twice.
note: Macro; the old contract was rejected for syntax, and the old prose ('2 raised to the field value times two') did not match the expression; values computed by hand from the expression.

name: static inline int nilfs_cpinfo_##name(const struct nilfs_cpinfo *cpinfo)
prose: Generated by NILFS_CPINFO_FNS(MINOR, minor) as nilfs_cpinfo_minor(cpinfo). It returns !!(cpinfo->ci_flags & (1UL << NILFS_CPINFO_MINOR)), that is 1 if bit NILFS_CPINFO_MINOR of ci_flags is set and 0 otherwise. In the checkpoint-flag enum NILFS_CPINFO_SNAPSHOT is 0, NILFS_CPINFO_INVALID is 1, NILFS_CPINFO_SKETCH is 2 and NILFS_CPINFO_MINOR is 3, so the bit tested is bit 3. It changes nothing.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose said bit 2; the enumerator values are SNAPSHOT 0, INVALID 1, SKETCH 2, MINOR 3 (slice enum at nilfs2_api.h 'checkpoint flags').

name: io_uring_mmap
prose: This is the definition used when CONFIG_MMU is not defined (the real name is io_uring_mmap; the packet name io_uring_mmap_nommu does not exist in the source). It returns 0 if is_nommu_shared_mapping(vma->vm_flags) is true and -EINVAL otherwise. It ignores file, takes no lock and changes nothing. With CONFIG_MMU the function of the same name is a different one: it takes ctx->mmap_lock, validates the request with io_uring_validate_mmap_request and maps the pages with vm_insert_pages.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose did not say that it is only the !CONFIG_MMU variant. Name corrected to the real function name.

name: io_uring_get_unmapped_area
prose: This is the definition used when CONFIG_MMU is not defined (the real name is io_uring_get_unmapped_area; io_uring_get_unmapped_area_nommu does not exist in the source). It takes ctx = file->private_data, acquires ctx->mmap_lock with guard(mutex) for the rest of the call, and calls io_uring_validate_mmap_request(file, pgoff, len). If that gives an error pointer it returns PTR_ERR of it (the validator yields -EINVAL if there is no region for the offset, if the region is not set (no pages), or if it was provided by userspace); otherwise it returns the region's kernel pointer (mr->ptr) cast to unsigned long. The lock is released on return and addr and flags are ignored. With CONFIG_MMU the function of the same name differs: it returns -EINVAL if addr is nonzero, returns -ENOMEM if validation fails, and returns the result of mm_get_unmapped_area.
note: Reviewer's points (MMU version requires addr == 0, returns -ENOMEM, returns mm_get_unmapped_area) describe the other variant, not this one; the old prose described the !CONFIG_MMU body correctly but did not state the config condition, now added. Name corrected to the real function name.
